Prevention: Avoid planting crucifers on a field with a history of black rot
Also locate seedbeds away from main production fields
This bacterial disease is seedborne so using clean seed is essential.
It is also easily spread by splashing water and insects
Plant on raised beds at a site with good drainage
Control weeds and avoid irrigating early in the day when dew is present or late in the day
Avoid injuries to plants when working at the nursery or field
Sterilize cutlasses and hoes after work using fire or 10% bleach solution
Remove crop debris after harvest and destroy
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: broccoli, brussel sprout, cabbage
Monitor nursery and fields regularly looking for yellow areas along the leaf edge.
These lessions expand from the edges to the leaf to the midrib giving a distinctive 'V' shaped lession with yellow margins and brown necrotic tissue in the centre
The veins of the leaves can also appear brown/black
Infected plants may be stunted and heads are smaller and outer leaves die
Direct Control: Rogue infected plants and destroy them by burying outside production fields
Begin application after transplants are set in
Kocide 2000, Champion 80) at 1.5-2.0g/L of water immediately symptoms are observed.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance, always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides of
Apply three times in a season at 7-10 day intervals.
Do not use the same chemical group continuously on the same farm.
